question: What is the very first sign of a pressure sore starting to form?

options.A: A deep open crater with exposed subcutaneous fat
options.B: A fluid-filled blister with dark purple discoloration
options.C: Complete skin death with black dry eschar
options.D: Non-blanching erythema over a bony prominence

explanation: Well done! If skin stays red and doesn't turn white when you press it over a bone, pressure damage is starting.

question: In a mass casualty incident, what does a RED triage tag mean?

options.A: Minor injuries that can wait until the end of the shift
options.B: Immediate life-threatening injuries with a high chance of survival
options.C: Injuries so severe that survival is unlikely
options.D: Deceased patients who need no further attention

explanation: Spot on! Red means urgent. It tells us the patient has a life-threatening problem that we can fix right now to save their life.

question: What lab results typically point to primary hypothyroidism?

options.A: High TSH and high Free T4
options.B: High TSH and low Free T4
options.C: Low TSH and high Free T4
options.D: Low TSH and low Free T4

explanation: Spot on! When the thyroid slows down, the pituitary panics and pumps out high TSH trying to wake it up, while actual Free T4 levels drop.

question: Why do nurses commonly use compresses in the ward?

options.A: To lower a patient's overall core body temperature rapidly
options.B: To replace the need for intravenous fluid resuscitation
options.C: To permanently cure chronic autoimmune joint diseases
options.D: To provide localized pain relief and reduce inflammation

explanation: Compresses are great for targeting one specific spot to ease pain and bring down swelling, rather than treating the whole body.

question: Why is simply giving people health facts often insufficient for changing their daily habits?

options.A: Medical facts are too complex for ordinary community members to understand.
options.B: Knowledge alone does not automatically translate into action without addressing cultural norms and barriers.
options.C: Patients usually forget health instructions within five minutes of hearing them.
options.D: People prefer to listen to traditional healers rather than trained nurses.

explanation: People often know what they should do, but social pressures, beliefs, and practical barriers prevent them from changing their behavior. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T2#GNS124_U5_T2_h3)

question: A patient suffers a severe spinal cord injury at the level of C2. What major complication do you anticipate?

options.A: Paralysis of the lower legs while retaining full upper body movement
options.B: Inability to move the facial muscles while breathing remains normal
options.C: Loss of sensation only in the hands and lower arms
options.D: Inability to breathe independently due to loss of phrenic nerve function

explanation: Since the phrenic nerve depends on C3 to C5 to function, an injury higher up at C2 cuts off the brain's breathing signals to the diaphragm. Patient safety first! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h4)

question: A patient shows signs of liver trouble after starting a new drug. Which of these should you NOT do?

options.A: Document the adverse event clearly in the patient record
options.B: Continue the medication at half the prescribed dose
options.C: Notify the attending physician immediately of the findings
options.D: Monitor liver function lab values closely per protocol

explanation: Never keep giving an idiosyncratic drug at a lower dose—these reactions don't depend on dose size and can still turn dangerous! Fantastic effort today.

question: What is the main job of proteins in our diet?

options.A: Simple sugars utilized strictly for immediate brain activity
options.B: Inorganic elements that regulate body fluid balance
options.C: Fatty acids stored directly in adipose tissue for insulation
options.D: Amino acids used for tissue construction and cellular repair

explanation: Think of proteins as your body's building blocks. They break down into amino acids to fix worn-out tissues and build new ones.

question: What does a psychoactive substance mainly do to the human body?

options.A: It permanently repairs damaged nerve tissues
options.B: It alters brain function and mental state
options.C: It lowers overall blood pressure immediately
options.D: It speeds up the process of digestion

explanation: Spot on! Psychoactive substances target the central nervous system, which changes how a person thinks, feels, and behaves. You've got this!

question: What is the main goal of building a safety culture in a hospital?

options.A: Ensuring hospitals meet strict financial profit margins
options.B: Reducing the total number of employed nursing personnel
options.C: Prioritizing patient protection from accidental harm above all else
options.D: Punishing staff members who make clinical errors

explanation: Spot on! A safety culture is all about putting patient safety first and making sure everyone works together to prevent accidental harm.

question: What is the typical pattern of pain experienced in the early stages of osteoarthritis?

options.A: Sudden sharp pain that only happens during deep sleep
options.B: Severe constant pain that never changes day or night
options.C: Pain that worsens with activity and gets better with rest
options.D: Pain that disappears completely when walking long distances

explanation: Early osteoarthritis pain is typically triggered by joint use and eased when the client rests the affected limb. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h3)

question: Why do we need to turn heavy research data into quick clinical guidelines for bedside nurses?

options.A: Guidelines replace the need for critical thinking in patient care
options.B: Bedside nurses are not allowed to look at original research data
options.C: Hospital policies forbid nurses from talking about academic studies
options.D: Clinicians rarely have time to read lengthy, complex research papers

explanation: Spot on! Busy clinical nurses are always on their feet and need quick, easy-to-digest summaries rather than long academic manuscripts.

question: What is the primary benefit of enrolling a patient in a structured cardiac rehabilitation program?

options.A: Providing a surgical alternative to coronary artery bypass grafting
options.B: Improving overall physical conditioning and reducing future heart risks
options.C: Ensuring the patient never has to take prescription medications again
options.D: Eliminating the need for routine follow-up visits with the cardiologist

explanation: Cardiac rehabilitation helps patients regain strength, manage risk factors, lower stress, and significantly reduce the likelihood of future cardiac events. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T13#GNS213_U1_T13_h6)

question: Which pathway carries nerve signals toward the central nervous system?

options.A: Sympathetic division
options.B: Efferent division
options.C: Afferent division
options.D: Autonomic division

explanation: A-fferent arrives at the brain (think 'A' for arrival). You'll master these terms in no time! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is the recommended period of sexual abstinence before providing a semen sample for analysis?

options.A: Exactly one month
options.B: Twelve to twenty-four hours
options.C: Two to seven days
options.D: One to two full weeks

explanation: A standard abstinence window of two to seven days ensures reliable sperm count and quality measurements. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h6)

question: Why is severe anemia especially dangerous for a woman going into labor?

options.A: She has very little reserve to survive normal blood loss during delivery
options.B: She will automatically develop eclampsia within hours
options.C: Her contractions will completely stop during the first stage
options.D: Her baby will be born with severe bone deformities

explanation: You're doing great! Every delivery involves some blood loss. A mom with low blood levels (anemia) cannot afford even a small loss without sliding into shock.

question: A patient is fitted with a vaginal pessary for a uterine prolapse. What key instruction must the nurse include in her discharge teaching?

options.A: Leave the device in place permanently without removal.
options.B: Report any unusual discharge, odor, or discomfort promptly.
options.C: Expect the pessary to cure the prolapse within one week.
options.D: Avoid all physical activity while the device is in place.

explanation: You got it! Pessaries need careful monitoring. Any strange discharge or odor is a red flag that could mean irritation or infection, so the patient must report it right away.

question: Which nutrient is especially helpful for building collagen and healing bones?

options.A: Vitamin K
options.B: Potassium
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Sodium

explanation: Vitamin C is a superstar for building collagen—the framework that new bone tissue needs to grow on!

question: Why is the hypophysial portal system so important for hormone control?

options.A: It allows brain hormones to reach the pituitary gland without being diluted in the main bloodstream
options.B: It cools down the hypothalamus when body temperature rises during a fever
options.C: It stores excess neurohormones until the body requires emergency fight-or-flight responses
options.D: It prevents hormones from the pituitary gland from entering the general circulation

explanation: This direct pathway acts like a private express lane, making sure brain hormones get straight to the pituitary gland in strong, concentrated doses without getting lost in the wider body circulation.

question: What is the primary objective of tertiary prevention?

options.A: Promoting healthy lifestyle habits in children
options.B: Screening healthy populations for early signs
options.C: Limiting disability and restoring function
options.D: Stopping initial exposure to a disease agent

explanation: Tertiary prevention focuses on managing existing chronic conditions to prevent complications and maximize remaining abilities. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which of these is a classic example of 'formal social control'?

options.A: Family members showing disappointment in a child
options.B: Neighbors gossiping about someone being rude
options.C: Police arrests and court fines for breaking laws
options.D: Community elders advising youth to behave well

explanation: That's right! Formal control uses official systems like laws, the police, and courts to keep order.

question: Which type of waste must be burned at very high temperatures instead of just going into an autoclave?

options.A: Cardboard medication delivery boxes
options.B: Empty intravenous fluid plastic bags
options.C: Pathological waste and human tissues
options.D: Uncontaminated paper paperwork

explanation: Anatomical parts and human tissues require high-temperature incineration for safety and out of respect for human dignity.

question: Why does Staphylococcus food poisoning cause sudden vomiting very soon after eating?

options.A: It blocks normal movement in the large intestine
options.B: It destroys the stomach lining with acid
options.C: It produces toxins in the food before you even eat it
options.D: It multiplies inside the bloodstream instantly

explanation: Think of Staph as leaving nasty toxins behind in food left out too long. Once you eat it, those pre-made toxins trigger rapid vomiting. Makes total sense, right?

question: Why do hospitals immediately isolate patients showing respiratory symptoms?

options.A: To speed up the administration of intravenous fluids
options.B: To reduce the cost of diagnostic testing supplies
options.C: To prevent transmission to staff and other patients
options.D: To allow patients to sleep without hospital noise

explanation: Isolating patients right away stops airborne droplets from spreading to other vulnerable people in the clinic. Smart nursing practice! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T12#GNS214_U1_T12_h4)

question: Why do victims of gender-based violence often fail to disclose their abuse during a routine medical visit?

options.A: They frequently present with vague physical complaints and fear judgment
options.B: They are usually unaware that physical injuries are linked to abuse
options.C: They prefer to discuss their problems only with law enforcement officers
options.D: Hospital policies strictly forbid nurses from asking about personal relationships

explanation: Victims often hide the root cause of their trauma due to fear, shame, or presenting with unrelated physical symptoms, requiring nurses to look beyond the surface. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T9#GNS312_U4_T9_h1)

question: Which of these is a very common fall hazard found in many homes?

options.A: Loose scatter rugs on polished floors
options.B: Low furniture located near the walls
options.C: Hardwood floors without any coverings
options.D: Bright lighting in the hallway stairs

explanation: Exactly! Unsecured rugs easily slip underfoot, making them a leading cause of accidental falls at home.

question: Which assessment gives the best practical idea of an older adult's functional independence?

options.A: Checking only the laboratory values for liver and kidney function
options.B: Evaluating the patient's ability to perform activities of daily living
options.C: Measuring the exact circumference of the upper arm muscles
options.D: Reviewing the family medical tree for inherited genetic conditions

explanation: Spot on! Checking how well a patient handles activities of daily living (ADLs) tells you real-world details about how safely they can live on their own.

question: A client stopped taking her oral contraceptive pills because she kept forgetting daily doses. What is a great alternative to suggest?

options.A: Switching to a long-acting method like an implant or injection
options.B: Stopping all contraception permanently without alternatives
options.C: Taking three pills at once every Sunday morning
options.D: Relying entirely on calendar guessing without records

explanation: Long-acting reversible contraceptives (LARCs) like implants or injections take the stress out of daily pill-taking!

question: Why do speech therapists and nurses sometimes add thickeners to drinks for dysphagia patients?

options.A: They slow down the flow rate to allow airway closure time
options.B: They prevent the liquid from tasting bitter to the patient
options.C: They provide extra calories and protein for wound healing
options.D: They stimulate the taste buds to increase appetite

explanation: Thin liquids rush down a weak throat way too fast before the epiglottis can close. Thickening the drink slows it down just enough for a safe swallow!

question: Why do teenage girls need more daily iron in their diet than younger children do?

options.A: To prevent soft bones from a lack of sunlight
options.B: To support monthly period blood loss and growing muscles
options.C: To maintain normal skin color and elasticity
options.D: To help digest heavy local meals easily

explanation: You nailed it! Monthly periods and rapid physical growth use up iron quickly, so eating more iron-rich foods helps prevent anemia.

question: What yummy nickname is often given to old, dark blood-filled cysts found on the ovaries in endometriosis?

options.A: Chocolate cysts
options.B: Serous cystadenomas
options.C: Dermoid tumors
options.D: Fibroid nodules

explanation: They are called 'chocolate cysts' because the old, trapped menstrual blood inside turns dark brown and thick, looking a bit like melted chocolate!

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for growing and branching the milk ducts during early development?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Progesterone
options.D: Prolactin

explanation: Estrogen acts like the master gardener, helping the milk duct system grow and branch out nicely inside the breast.

question: What is the main goal of isolation tactics used in emotional abuse?

options.A: To help the victim save money by avoiding social gatherings
options.B: To encourage the victim to focus more on their personal career goals
options.C: To protect the victim from catching infectious community diseases
options.D: To increase the victim's dependence by cutting off their support systems

explanation: Abusers isolate victims from friends and family to make them completely dependent and reduce their chances of seeking help. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T9#GNS312_U4_T9_h3)

question: How do humans usually catch hydatid disease?

options.A: Bites from infected mosquitoes
options.B: Inhalation of airborne cyst spores
options.C: Fecal-oral ingestion of parasite eggs
options.D: Direct skin penetration by larvae

explanation: It usually happens by accidentally swallowing microscopic eggs from dog feces via contaminated food, water, or unwashed hands.

question: What is the main reason nurses use functional assessment tools in rehab?

options.A: To calculate the exact date a patient will leave the hospital
options.B: To diagnose the exact strain of bacteria causing an infection
options.C: To determine the financial cost of hospital stay
options.D: To measure a patient's ability to perform activities of daily living

explanation: Assessment scales give nurses an easy way to track how well a patient is managing basic self-care tasks over time.

question: A patient eats shrimp, gets hives, swollen lips, and a dangerous drop in blood pressure. What caused the blood pressure to drop so fast?

options.A: Sudden slowing of the electrical heart rhythm
options.B: Massive peripheral blood vessel dilation
options.C: Rapid clotting of blood inside the major veins
options.D: Severe internal bleeding from the stomach

explanation: Histamine relaxes blood vessels all over the body at once. When they open up too wide, blood pressure plummets—that's distributive shock!

question: Why is it important for an objective to be 'Achievable' rather than impossible to reach?

options.A: To stretch the team without causing exhaustion and burnout.
options.B: To make sure work is completed twice as fast.
options.C: To ensure the hospital avoids spending any money at all.
options.D: To eliminate the need for any staff supervision.

explanation: We want goals that challenge us to grow, but setting impossible bars only leads to frustration and burnout. Balance is key!

question: What major mistake should you avoid when collecting a swab sample?

options.A: Using a transport tube that is completely clear of liquid
options.B: Parting the labia majora gently with the non-dominant hand
options.C: Touching the surrounding skin and contaminating the swab
options.D: Rotating the swab against the surface of the lesion too long

explanation: Be careful! Touching normal skin introduces random bacteria that can mess up the test and hide the real cause of the infection.

question: What is the most important first step when assessing a newly met street child?

options.A: Building trust through a non-judgmental and patient approach
options.B: Documenting their home address for official taxation
options.C: Immediately calling law enforcement to detain the minor
options.D: Insisting on immediate blood draws for laboratory tests

explanation: Brilliant nursing logic! Because these kids are used to being mistreated, you have to win their trust before they will let you help them.

question: Which of these patients is most at risk of catching a hospital infection?

options.A: A middle-aged nurse working full-time in the surgical ward
options.B: A healthy outpatient visiting the clinic for a routine checkup
options.C: A young adult recovering from a simple sprained ankle
options.D: An elderly patient receiving chemotherapy and using a urinary catheter

explanation: Exactly. Between age, chemotherapy lowering their immunity, and a catheter creating an easy entry path, this patient's defenses are stretched thin.

question: How do the kidneys balance out the mild breathing changes (respiratory alkalosis) that happen during pregnancy?

options.A: By excreting more bicarbonate in the urine
options.B: By shutting down the production of red blood cells
options.C: By storing extra carbon dioxide in the renal pelvis
options.D: By absorbing more sodium from the renal tubules

explanation: To keep the body's acid-base balance just right when a mum breathes a bit faster, the kidneys simply let go of some extra bicarbonate in the urine. Brilliant teamwork by the body systems!

question: Why is it clinically important for nurses to separate biological sex from gender?

options.A: Gender is the only factor that matters for prescribing medications safely
options.B: Biological sex has no impact on a person's health outcomes whatsoever
options.C: Physical examinations are entirely unrelated to the concept of gender
options.D: Patients have both biological health needs and social experiences that affect care

explanation: Recognizing both biological and social dimensions ensures that nurses address the complete health profile of every patient without making false assumptions. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h2)

question: A patient with severe asthma gets wheezing after eating certain preserved foods. Which additive should you teach them to avoid?

options.A: Sulfites
options.B: Plain yeast
options.C: Fresh vitamins
options.D: Natural water

explanation: Sulfites are chemical preservatives well known for triggering asthma flare-ups and allergic reactions in sensitive people.

question: What does the term 'legal liability' mean in nursing practice?

options.A: Being legally responsible for one's professional actions and omissions
options.B: The right to sue a client for refusing prescribed medication
options.C: The obligation to pay taxes on monthly nursing salaries
options.D: Having absolute immunity from all criminal charges in court

explanation: Liability means accountability under the law for the duties performed or neglected during professional practice. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h6)

question: Which circumcision tool uses a small plastic ring tied over the foreskin that eventually falls off on its own?

options.A: Plastibell
options.B: Gomco clamp
options.C: Scalpel blade
options.D: Mogen clamp

question: What kind of dressing is typically placed over the needle site once the catheter is removed?

options.A: An airtight plastic wrap
options.B: A standard elastic bandage
options.C: A wet saline gauze wrap
options.D: A sterile pressure dressing

explanation: A pressure dressing helps close up the tiny puncture wound and stops ongoing leaking or bleeding.

question: Why is giving people only cheap, starchy food not enough for long-term health?

options.A: It cannot be stored in community kitchens
options.B: It causes immediate starvation within a few hours
options.C: It is always more expensive than fresh vegetables
options.D: It does not prevent micronutrient deficiencies or hidden hunger

explanation: Well reasoned! While starch gives energy, true health needs a balance of vitamins, minerals, and proteins to keep deficiency diseases away.

question: What major economic challenge often pushes desperate families toward child traffickers?

options.A: Widespread poverty and lack of basic needs
options.B: Abundant job opportunities in local markets
options.C: Strict government taxes on large families
options.D: Excessive wealth in rural farming villages

explanation: When families struggle to put food on the table, traffickers easily trick parents by promising money or a better future for their kids.

question: A clinic has enough money for either a new blood-pressure machine or routine infant vaccines. As a public health nurse, what should you prioritize?

options.A: Save the money in a personal bank account until next year
options.B: The routine infant vaccines to prevent infectious disease outbreaks
options.C: Split the money evenly to buy broken office furniture
options.D: The blood pressure machine because adult patients complain more

question: Which type of mental ability actually tends to stay stable or even improve as people grow older?

options.A: Physical reaction speed during sudden emergency events
options.B: Crystallized intelligence based on accumulated life experience
options.C: Short-term working memory for complex math equations
options.D: Immediate recall of random, unrelated lists of numbers

explanation: Wisdom comes with age! Crystallized intelligence relies on stored knowledge and life experience, which stays strong or even grows as people get older.

question: What is septicemia?

options.A: Presence of multiplying bacteria in the bloodstream
options.B: Inflammation limited to the outer layer of skin
options.C: A localized collection of pus in a single muscle
options.D: Sudden paralysis caused by a damaged nerve

explanation: Septicemia happens when bacteria get past local defenses and start multiplying in the general blood circulation, making the patient very ill all over.

question: What is a very common challenge when trying to introduce quality improvement in a busy Nigerian ward?

options.A: Staff burnout and resistance to new routines
options.B: Patients demanding too many safety checklists
options.C: An excess of extra nursing staff on every shift
options.D: Doctors writing too many clear care instructions

explanation: So true! When nurses are already tired and overworked from busy shifts, asking them to learn brand new routines can be tough. We have to support each other!

question: What is the heart of constructivist learning theory?

options.A: Behavior changes only occur through strict reward systems
options.B: Knowledge is an exact copy of what the textbook states
options.C: Learners actively build new knowledge using past experiences
options.D: Students learn best when they sit quietly and listen to lectures

explanation: You aren't just an empty bucket waiting to be filled! Constructivism means you connect new nursing concepts to what you already know from your own life and experiences.

question: What term describes the wear and tear on the body from long-term, ongoing stress?

options.A: Systemic exhaustion
options.B: Adverse adaptation
options.C: Allostatic load
options.D: Homeostatic balance

explanation: 'Allostatic load' is just a fancy way of saying your body gets tired and worn down from fighting stress day after day without a break.

question: An asthma patient says they need to use their rescue inhaler every single day for wheezing. What does this tell you?

options.A: The patient is experiencing a normal, expected reaction to therapy
options.B: The spacer device is broken and needs to be replaced immediately
options.C: The patient is using the correct technique for daily maintenance
options.D: The underlying disease is poorly controlled and needs medical review

explanation: Needing a rescue inhaler more than twice a week is a red flag that the asthma isn't well-controlled, meaning the doctor needs to review their daily maintenance plan.

question: Why do babies need other foods (complementary feeding) introduced around six months of age?

options.A: Breast milk alone can no longer meet all growing nutritional needs
options.B: Babies automatically reject breast milk once teeth begin to erupt
options.C: Maternal antibodies completely disappear from the mother's milk
options.D: The baby stops producing digestive enzymes for milk proteins

explanation: Correct! As babies grow fast at this stage, they need extra iron and energy that breast milk alone can't fully cover anymore.

question: What is the primary goal of secondary prevention in healthcare?

options.A: Long-term physical rehabilitation
options.B: Early detection and treatment
options.C: Providing end-of-life comfort care
options.D: Stopping disease before it starts

explanation: Secondary prevention catches health issues early through screening so treatment can stop the disease from getting worse. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h1)

question: Where does the normal electrical spark for every heartbeat start?

options.A: Bundle of His
options.B: Atrioventricular node
options.C: Sinoatrial node
options.D: Purkinje fibers

explanation: The sinoatrial (SA) node is the heart's natural pacemaker, setting the steady rhythm for every beat you take!

question: When summarizing key results for a study on preventing pressure sores, what belongs right at the start?

options.A: Detailed instructions on how to use turning sheets
options.B: A complete list of every patient's medical history
options.C: Raw survey responses from all participating nurses
options.D: The main answer to the primary research question

explanation: You're crushing it! Always address the main question first so your reader immediately knows what the study found.

question: How does Rifampicin stop TB bacteria from multiplying?

options.A: By dissolving the patient's lung tissue
options.B: By inhibiting bacterial RNA synthesis
options.C: By destroying the human liver cells
options.D: By blocking human vitamin absorption

explanation: Rifampicin targets bacterial RNA synthesis, halting the germ's ability to make essential proteins and grow.

question: Which color of waste bag is standard for infectious clinical waste and pathological specimens?

options.A: Yellow
options.B: Blue
options.C: Clear
options.D: Black

explanation: Yellow bags and bins are globally recognized for infectious and pathological waste that requires incineration. [learn more](GST114_U2_T14#GST114_U2_T14_h3)

question: Why might a financially dependent housewife hesitate to disclose her HIV status to her husband?

options.A: She fears losing her financial support and home if he reacts with anger or abandonment
options.B: She knows her husband already takes antiretroviral medications secretly
options.C: She is legally prohibited from speaking to her spouse about medical issues
options.D: She believes her husband will automatically cure the virus with traditional herbs

explanation: Economic vulnerability heavily complicates disclosure because patients worry about survival if rejection leads to destitution. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h5)

question: Which sign strongly points to an infection after a vasectomy?

options.A: Temporary discomfort when wearing loose underwear
options.B: A small, painless pea-sized lump near the cut end
options.C: Mild bruising and a dull pulling ache in the groin
options.D: Fever and pus draining from the scrotal incision

explanation: Brilliant! Fever and pus are classic warning signs of a bacterial infection that needs quick medical attention.

question: Why do midwives give a routine injection of Vitamin K to newborns shortly after delivery?

options.A: To improve digestion of breastmilk
options.B: To build strong bones and teeth
options.C: To protect against childhood infections
options.D: To prevent dangerous bleeding disorders

explanation: Babies are born with very low levels of Vitamin K and sterile tummies, which puts them at risk of bleeding until their gut flora kicks in. The injection protects them safely!

question: If a patient has too much sodium in their blood, where does water naturally rush to?

options.A: Out of the blood vessels completely through the skin
options.B: From the interstitial spaces into the lymphatic system
options.C: From the extracellular space directly into the cells
options.D: From inside the cells into the extracellular space

explanation: Water loves to follow salt! High sodium outside pulls water right out of the cells, making them shrink. Physics and nursing working together!

question: When is the right time to apply suction during tracheostomy suctioning?

options.A: While pushing the catheter down into the airway
options.B: Continuously throughout the entire procedure
options.C: Only while withdrawing and rotating the catheter
options.D: Before inserting any tubing into the stoma

explanation: Never apply suction on the way in! You only suction gently while twisting and pulling the catheter out to protect the delicate airway lining.

question: During a sterile procedure, a sterile instrument slips and drops below the level of the tabletop. What should you do?

options.A: Ask another staff member if they saw it touch the floor
options.B: Pick it up quickly and use it if it looks clean
options.C: Consider it contaminated and discard it
options.D: Wipe it with an antiseptic wipe before continuing

explanation: You got it! If an item drops below your waist or out of your direct sight, you can't guarantee its sterility anymore. Toss it out!

question: How long should a patient rest quietly before having their blood pressure measured?

options.A: Exactly 30 seconds
options.B: At least 5 minutes
options.C: No rest is needed
options.D: At least 1 hour

explanation: A short resting period ensures that recent physical activity or rushing does not falsely elevate the blood pressure reading. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h3)

question: What is the big advantage of partnering with local transport unions during a disaster?

options.A: Financing the national budget for disaster management
options.B: Securing vehicles quickly for evacuation and relief supply delivery
options.C: Exempting commercial drivers from all traffic laws permanently
options.D: Allowing union members to take over government leadership roles

explanation: Spot on! Transport unions have plenty of vehicles and know the local shortcuts, which speeds up evacuations and getting supplies where they need to go.

question: A patient spends hours washing their hands until the skin is raw, driven by a deep fear of germs. What does this behavior represent?

options.A: A somatic symptom disorder caused by nerve damage
options.B: A psychotic delusion regarding skin parasites
options.C: A compulsion driven by an obsession with contamination
options.D: Normal hygienic practice during an infection outbreak

explanation: Correct! The excessive washing is a physical compulsion born out of an overwhelming fear of getting contaminated.

question: Why do lab workers pass an inoculation loop through a Bunsen burner flame until it glows?

options.A: To cool down the loop before touching liquid samples
options.B: To kill any microorganisms currently on the loop
options.C: To make the metal bendable for easy scooping
options.D: To paint a protective coating onto the wire tip

explanation: Correct! Extreme heat quickly destroys any living germs or spores on the wire, leaving it completely sterile for your next step.

question: What is the primary pigment responsible for protecting skin cell DNA from ultraviolet damage?

options.A: Carotene
options.B: Hemoglobin
options.C: Bilirubin
options.D: Melanin

explanation: Melanin is produced by melanocytes to absorb UV radiation and shield the DNA in underlying skin cells from mutation. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h7)

question: Why is patient safety in maternity care uniquely complex?

options.A: Pregnancy completely prevents any physical or medical complications
options.B: The nurse must monitor and protect two distinct lives at the same time
options.C: Labor and delivery wards never experience staffing shortages
options.D: Maternity patients never follow clinical instructions or take medications

explanation: In maternity care, you are caring for both the mother and the baby. That doubles your watch duty and your clinical responsibility!

question: What is the main sign that a patient is truly unconscious?

options.A: A state of deep sleep that ends easily with noise
options.B: Total unresponsiveness to environmental stimuli
options.C: Inability to speak while remaining fully awake
options.D: Temporary dizziness upon standing up quickly

explanation: You've got this! Unconsciousness simply means the person cannot respond at all to what is happening around them. Keep going!

question: Why are healthcare workers sometimes at higher risk for developing substance use issues?

options.A: They are completely exempt from the legal penalties of drug abuse
options.B: They experience heavy job stress and have easy access to medications
options.C: They receive special training on how to safely consume illegal substances
options.D: They possess a genetic immunity that makes them careless with drugs

explanation: The intense stress of clinical life combined with being around drugs all day creates a tough environment. Looking out for our mental health as nurses is so important!

question: A patient in skeletal traction suddenly complains of severe pain and numb toes in the affected leg. What should you do first?

options.A: Check the equipment alignment and notify the physician immediately
options.B: Increase the hanging weight to relieve pressure
options.C: Give a sleeping pill and turn the patient on their side
options.D: Remove the skeletal traction pin at the bedside

explanation: Great clinical thinking! Sudden pain and numbness mean blood flow or nerves might be squeezed. Always check the setup first and call the doctor right away.

question: What is the medical term used when a patient's bad reaction stops after the suspected drug is withdrawn?

options.A: Tolerance
options.B: Anaphylaxis
options.C: Dechallenge
options.D: Rechallenge

explanation: Think of 'dechallenge' as un-challenging the body—stopping the medicine to see if the symptoms get better or go away.

question: How does boosting a patient's understanding of food directly help their health?

options.A: It cures all existing vitamin deficiencies overnight
options.B: It stops the body from absorbing excess dietary fats
options.C: It empowers them to make healthier food choices on their own
options.D: It eliminates the need to ever consult a doctor again

explanation: Exactly! When patients truly understand the 'why' behind good food, they are much happier to change their habits willingly, without you standing over them.

question: What is the main goal of adaptive processes in our body and mind?

options.A: To eliminate all forms of emotional memory
options.B: To increase physical heart rate permanently
options.C: To prevent any future exposure to conflict
options.D: To restore internal balance during stress

explanation: Think of adaptive processes like your body's natural shock absorbers. They kick in to help you handle stress and bring your inner calm back!

question: Which of these is allowed on a full fluid diet, but NOT on a clear fluid diet?

options.A: Plain water
options.B: Transparent beef broth
options.C: Clear apple juice
options.D: Plain milk

explanation: Clear fluids you can see straight through (like water or broth). Full fluids include cloudy items like milk and custard!

question: What do anticoagulant medications actually do in the body?

options.A: Make the circulating blood thicker
options.B: Dissolve existing blood clots completely
options.C: Stop platelets from clumping together
options.D: Prevent the formation of new blood clots

explanation: Think of anticoagulants as your body's stop sign for new clots. They don't break down clots that are already there, but they stop new ones from forming or getting bigger!

question: What does the acronym PAIR stand for in the management of hydatid cysts?

options.A: Preparation, Anesthesia, Isolation, Recovery
options.B: Puncture, Aspiration, Injection, Respiration
options.C: Palpation, Auscultation, Incusion, Repair
options.D: Perfusion, Activation, Irrigation, Removal

explanation: PAIR is a percutaneous technique involving puncturing the cyst, aspirating fluid, injecting a scolicidal agent, and reaspirating. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T25#GNS313_U2_T25_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT an appropriate nursing action regarding cultural healing practices?

options.A: Collaborating gently with community health beliefs
options.B: Asking respectfully about previous treatments tried
options.C: Providing education on psychiatric medication benefits
options.D: Mocking or insulting the client's traditional beliefs

explanation: Nurses must never mock or insult cultural beliefs, as this destroys trust and drives patients away from healthcare services. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T6#GNS314_U4_T6_h6)

question: What is the recommended infant feeding practice for mothers living on ART where replacement feeding is unsafe?

options.A: Exclusive use of herbal teas and plain water
options.B: Immediate weaning onto cow milk on day one
options.C: Strict formula feeding without any breast milk
options.D: Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding combined with maternal ART provides the best balance of nutrition and protection against HIV transmission. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h7)

question: During a home visit in a rural village, a nurse has to make important care decisions independently. Which nursing field is this?

options.A: Operating theatre nursing
options.B: Intensive care unit nursing
options.C: Community health nursing
options.D: Central sterile supply nursing

explanation: Exactly! Out in the field, community nurses often work on their own, trusting their training and assessment skills to make great clinical choices.

question: What is an important task for school management when evaluating their health programme?

options.A: Reviewing clinic attendance logs to spot health trends
options.B: Changing the academic grading system every term
options.C: Firing teachers who report sick with malaria
options.D: Keeping all student medical records strictly secret from staff

explanation: Exactly! Checking clinic records helps leaders spot recurring health issues early and take quick, smart action.

question: What main process causes tissue damage inside the pancreas during acute pancreatitis?

options.A: Infection of pancreatic tissue by gut bacteria traveling upward
options.B: Rapid formation of scar tissue blocking the pancreatic duct
options.C: Autodigestion of the pancreas by its own early-activated enzymes
options.D: Complete lack of blood supply caused by sudden heart failure

explanation: Think of it as friendly fire! Digestive enzymes turn on too early while still inside the pancreas, and they accidentally start breaking down the organ's own tissue.

question: What is a major characteristic of passive immunity?

options.A: It stimulates the bone marrow to produce permanent memory cells.
options.B: It only occurs after a patient recovers from a severe viral illness.
options.C: It provides immediate protection that fades relatively quickly.
options.D: It requires the body several weeks to manufacture its own T-cells.

explanation: Passive immunity gives you ready-made antibodies right away, but it wears off because your body didn't make memory cells.

question: Which part of the brainstem contains the centers that control your heart rate and breathing?

options.A: Midbrain
options.B: Corpus callosum
options.C: Thalamus
options.D: Medulla oblongata

explanation: The medulla oblongata keeps you alive by automatically running vital functions like your heartbeat and breathing rhythm.

question: What is the main benefit of Continuing Professional Development (CPD) for nurses?

options.A: It keeps nursing skills updated for modern and complex client needs
options.B: It serves as a punishment for making minor documentation errors
options.C: It allows nurses to work indefinitely without taking rest breaks
options.D: It replaces the need for initial professional nursing licensure

explanation: CPD keeps your nursing toolkit fresh! It ensures you stay up to date with new medical practices, technologies, and guidelines.

question: What is a common healthcare habit among many patients in Nigeria regarding traditional and modern hospital care?

options.A: Using both traditional and orthodox systems, sometimes concurrently
options.B: Using exclusively orthodox hospitals and completely ignoring local herbs
options.C: Relying entirely on foreign imported medications
options.D: Consulting spiritual healers only after death has occurred

explanation: Correct! Many people naturally blend traditional remedies with modern hospital treatments in their daily lives.

question: What do the intervals or 'bins' on the horizontal axis represent in a histogram?

options.A: The specific dates when the study ended
options.B: Randomly selected patient interview questions
options.C: Different hospital wards in the facility
options.D: Equal numerical ranges of the measured variable

explanation: Bins cut the continuous scale into neat, equal slices so you can easily count and compare your data.
